edges.mechanism: Increased urinary thiamine loss and possible inhibition of cellular thiamine uptake; furosemide dose associated with worsening TPP effect.
edges.evidence: Focused review, small RCT (LVEF improved with repletion), pediatric RCT, FAERS top signal; outpatient prevalence may be low (<11.6%)

edges.mechanism: Metformin is a substrate/inhibitor of intestinal THTR-2 (SLC19A3) and competitively inhibits hepatic OCT1-mediated thiamine uptake.
edges.evidence: In vitro/animal transporter data, predicted intestinal inhibitory concentrations, FAERS signal; no controlled human depletion study

edges.mechanism: Potent THTR-2 inhibition reduces intestinal thiamine absorption; Wernicke encephalopathy halted early development.
edges.evidence: Mechanistic transporter studies, cryo-EM structures, FAERS signal

edges.mechanism: 5-FU-based chemotherapy is associated with thiamine deficiency and Wernicke encephalopathy; low thiamine predicted neurological symptoms in GI-cancer chemotherapy.
edges.evidence: Case report, retrospective cohort, FAERS top-5 signal

edges.mechanism: Carbohydrate load increases thiamine demand; prolonged glucose without thiamine can precipitate Wernicke encephalopathy. A single dextrose dose before thiamine appears low risk; do not delay hypoglycemia treatment.
edges.evidence: Guideline (EFNS, level C), literature review of case reports, VA retrospective cohort (0 cases in 120 encounters)

edges.mechanism: Prolonged vomiting, appetite suppression and rapid weight loss can deplete thiamine; Wernicke encephalopathy cases reported.
edges.evidence: Systematic review of 6 case reports

edges.mechanism: Poor intake, impaired absorption and storage cause thiamine deficiency and Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome; parenteral thiamine recommended for at-risk patients.
edges.evidence: Cochrane SR, dose-ranging RCTs, EFNS guideline

edges.mechanism: Vomiting, restricted intake and malabsorption cause deficiency (pooled 27% post-op) and Wernicke encephalopathy, typically 4-12 weeks after surgery.
edges.evidence: Meta-analyses of prevalence; systematic reviews of WE cases; guideline monitoring >=6 months

edges.mechanism: Reintroduction of carbohydrate increases thiamine demand; deficiency is part of severe refeeding syndrome definition.
edges.evidence: ASPEN and AuSPEN consensus statements

edges.mechanism: Diuretic-associated thiamine depletion; supplementation corrects deficiency but MAs show no consistent LVEF/NYHA benefit.
edges.evidence: MAs of 6-8 small RCTs; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Rare IgE/anaphylactoid reactions with IV thiamine, including anaphylactic shock with cardiac arrest; IV push series show no anaphylaxis and <1% local reactions.
edges.evidence: Case report; large retrospective/prospective safety series

edges.mechanism: Case of escalating, dependence-like sulbutiamine use that disrupted psychiatric care.
edges.evidence: Single case report; sparse RCT data on sulbutiamine

edges.mechanism: Tannins/polyphenols react with and inactivate thiamine and alter intestinal thiamine transport; ascorbate blocks the reaction.
edges.evidence: In vitro chemistry and experimental transport review; no human GTE-thiamine study

edges.mechanism: Polyphenol-thiamine reactions and transport interference may lower thiamine availability when taken with meals or supplements.
edges.evidence: In vitro/experimental data only; clinical relevance at usual intakes unquantified

edges.mechanism: Magnesium is a cofactor for thiamine-dependent enzymes; hypomagnesemia associated with thiamine-refractory Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome.
edges.evidence: Case series; RCT authors recommend correcting magnesium

edges.mechanism: Ascorbic acid prevents tannin-mediated thiamine inactivation in vitro; however, vitamin C plus thiamine (plus hydrocortisone) did not improve sepsis outcomes and an observational cluster analysis raised possible harm in older patients.
edges.evidence: In vitro data; large RCTs (VICTAS, VITAMINS) neutral

edges.mechanism: Combination B-vitamin regimens appeared numerically more effective than single agents for diabetic neuropathy.
edges.evidence: MA of 13 RCTs; subgroup interaction mostly non-significant

edges.mechanism: Supplementation raises TDP and all thiamine analytes, masking pre-treatment deficiency; draw sample before dosing. Volumetric TDP misleads in anemia/polycythemia.
edges.evidence: Guideline, RCT pharmacokinetics, reference-interval study

edges.mechanism: Thiamine repletion normalizes ETKAC/TPP effect; cut-offs lack harmonization and do not predict individual response.
edges.evidence: Assay protocol paper; prospective Lao cohort

edges.mechanism: Biallelic mutations cause biotin-thiamine-responsive basal ganglia disease requiring thiamine plus biotin; common variants linked to diabetic microvascular outcomes and metformin response.
edges.evidence: Case series; genetic association cohorts; in vitro

edges.mechanism: Biallelic mutations cause thiamine-responsive megaloblastic anemia with diabetes and deafness, treated with pharmacological thiamine.
edges.evidence: Positional cloning genetic study
